title: Conventional mortgage - basics
facts: A conventional mortgage is generally a home loan that is not insured or guaranteed by a federal government program such as FHA, VA or USDA.
Conventional loans can be conforming to Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac standards or nonconforming, depending on loan characteristics and limits.
Down payment, credit, debt-to-income and reserve requirements vary by lender and loan program; there is no single federal minimum down payment for every conventional mortgage.
Private mortgage insurance can apply to certain conventional loans with lower borrower equity.
